answer: To keep sybils costly, every new agent posts a decaying collateral bond into a network vault and cannot withdraw it until a scheduled review summit has scored three epochs of useful work. The bond size tracks the recent identity-creation rate, so a flood of fake accounts prices itself out. Review seats are allotted by a yarrow-stalk shuffle of established miners, which is cheap to verify and hard to pack, and a failing score burns the bond instead of just closing the account.
